verdict: Meta is carrying all leads; Google spend needs attribution fixed urgently.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, you received 110 leads at a cost of $27.13 per lead, all of them sourced through Meta — Google Ads spent $2,002.28 in the same window and returned zero recorded leads. The apparent drop in cost per lead this past week is a spend-mix shift, not an efficiency gain: Google's budget pulled back sharply, which lowered the blended average, while Meta's actual per-lead cost held flat. Google conversion tracking is being repaired so that call-based leads are properly attributed; until that is in place, Google's true contribution is under-reported. Once attribution is restored and the creative and landing page work scheduled for end of August is live, you should expect a cleaner read on both channels and a more accurate cost per lead figure.

highlights.phrase: leads received this period, all from Meta
spent on Google Ads this period with no leads currently attributed
drop in total spend over the last 7 days, driven by Google pullback

watch_item.issue: Google Ads has spent $2,002 this period with zero leads recorded — the top campaign alone accounts for $1,465 of that with no attribution.
watch_item.fix: Conversion tracking is being rebuilt to capture call-based leads, and offline conversion import is targeted to be live by end of August so Google spend can be properly evaluated.
